sources.title: SELECTIVE AND ADAPTIVE RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION WITH CONTEXT COMPRESSION [WO2026241334A1]
sources.abstract: Methods and systems related to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are disclosed. Context data elements (e.g., digital documents from a database or "chunks" of documents) that are relevant to a query can be identified. Primary context data elements and secondary context data elements can be determined from these context data elements. Generally, the primary context data elements can comprise context data elements that are more relevant to the query, and the secondary context data elements can be less relevant (but still relevant) to the query. A prompt can be generated that contains the query, the primary context data elements in textual form, and compression vectors representative of the secondary context data elements. This prompt and a foundation model (e.g., a large language model) can be used to generate a query response. The combination of textual and compressed context balances high performance and reduced token consumption (for token-based foundation models).

sources.title: METHOD FOR COMMISSIONING A RAG SYSTEM [WO2026241009A1]
sources.abstract: A method for commissioning an RAG system with a neural network and a knowledge graph which comprises generating test case outputs and processing them by a failure evaluation engine. The failure evaluation comprises a plurality of different failure metric algorithms, each configured to generate a different test result rating. The test result ratings are processed through a failure classification algorithm to classify a test result dataset that comprises the test result ratings. The failure classification algorithm takes a use case dataset for each test case output into account to classify the test result dataset. The test result ratings are continuous values.

sources.title: ROBOT CONTROL DEVICE [WO2026239561A1]
sources.abstract: The present invention makes it possible to execute a robot task operation corresponding to a real environment without retraining a large language model. This robot control device comprises: a bounding box information acquisition unit that acquires, through an object detector, bounding box information which is information about a bounding box surrounding an object depicted in an image, for a target object on which the robot performs task operation and an object of the robot which acts on said target object; and an operation trajectory acquisition unit that acquires an operation trajectory of the robot in a real space, the operation trajectory being generated on the basis of operation examples compatible with the bounding box information using a large language model system that utilizes, as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), a database in which operation examples of the robot are stored.

sources.title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR CLASSIFYING AND ANNOTATING ENTITIES FROM IMAGES [US20260369036A1]
sources.abstract: The disclosure relates to a method and a system for classifying and annotating entities from images within an environment. The method includes acquiring image data representing entities using at least one imaging device, followed by determining spatial relationships between the entities. A simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) module processes the spatial relationships to generate a three-dimensional (3D) representation of the environment. Entity attributes are then extracted from the 3D representation using a trained model incorporating domain-specific templates. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agentic system further analyzes the extracted attributes to identify the types and characteristics of the entities. Based on this identification, the entities are classified and annotated to enable structured representation and efficient organization. The method enhances entity recognition accuracy by integrating depth sensing, AI-driven classification, and contextual retrieval, making it applicable to various industries, including industrial automation, infrastructure monitoring, and digital asset management.

sources.title: Clustering Multi-Vector Embeddings for Denoising and Pruning [US20260368643A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems can generate multi-vector embeddings of content items, reduce the number of vectors by clustering them, and then using the resulting compressed representations for retrieval tasks. For example, a machine-learned multi-vector embedding model can process a content item to create multiple vectors that each represent a portion (e.g., a token) of the item. The system can then cluster these vectors into a smaller set for more compact storage in a retrieval index. Additionally, the system can compute similarity scores (e.g., Chamfer distance) between the compressed embedding sets and embedding(s) associated with an input content item (which may themselves be optionally compressed as described herein). The computing system can select (e.g., rank) candidate items that best align with the input content item based on the computed similarity scores. This approach can be beneficial for deployment in scenarios like large-scale web search, image or audio search, retrieval-augmented generation, and/or other applications.

sources.title: APPARATUSES AND METHODS FOR FACILITATING A DYNAMIC RADIO ACCESS NETWORK WITH RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION FOR SATELLITE GEO-LOCATION [US20260370323A1]
sources.abstract: Aspects of the subject disclosure may include, for example, obtaining first data pertaining to a load that is to be accommodated by terrestrial network infrastructure, analyzing the first data via a model, determining, based on the analyzing, that the load exceeds a threshold, identifying, based on the determining, at least one satellite that is available to support a portion of the load, selecting, based on the identifying, a satellite included in the at least one satellite, resulting in a selected satellite, establishing a connection with the selected satellite, and facilitating a transfer of second data over the connection to facilitate a communication service associated with the load. Other embodiments are disclosed.

sources.title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR TESTING AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) AND GENERATIVE AI APPLICATION [US20260368077A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    The present invention relates to a system (102) for testing the AI and Gen AI applications comprising the user interface (302) configured to enable interaction with the user and facilitate access to the plurality of modules, API's (304), playbooks (308), tools (310), demo module (312), assets, and playgrounds (316). The plurality of API's (304) comprises a functional APIs, plurality of non-functional APIs, and plurality of governance APIs. The plurality of tools (310) selected from the group consisting of test-driven RAG development tool, automated multi-agent system tool, non-functional LLM testing tool, LLM security testing tool, integration and monitoring dashboard, and guardrails, and configured to perform automated RAG evaluation, agentic supervision testing, non-functional LLM testing, and security testing using adversarial prompt generation. The system (102) is configured to evaluate, validate, and test applications using the plurality of tools (310) and API's (304).

sources.title: INTENT-SYNTHESIZED BIDIRECTIONAL EMBEDDING SEARCHES [US20260368230A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    The systems and methods disclosed herein execute intent-synthesized bidirectional embedding searches. A query is received from a user interface. The systems and methods generate/determine (e.g., via an AI model and/or user input) a label for the query and construct a training dataset of synthetic artifacts (e.g., results, data). A linear model is trained using the training dataset to determine a vector representation of the expected output of the query. Thus, the linear model can be used to select non-synthetic artifacts (e.g., data) from a vector database based on a similarity between the vector representations of each non-synthetic artifact and the expected output. Thus, when a new artifact is added, matching queries can be identified based on a similarity between the vector representations of the new artifact and the queries.

sources.title: AUTOMATED DOCUMENT PLANNING AND REPORT GENERATION [US20260368233A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems and methods for automated report generation using large language models (LLMs). The LLMs may receive an intent of a report from a user and perform an electronic resource review process based on the received intent. The review process may generate initial queries based on the intent and search one or more data sources using the initial queries. The retrieved documents may be used to generate a vector database and complementary search indexes. Outlines for the retrieved documents may be extracted and used to generate a report outline corresponding to an output report to be generated. The LLMs may perform a recursive question expansion process based on the intent and the extracted outlines. The LLMs may then be prompted to generate an output report based on answers from the recursive question expansion process and generated report outline. Output generation may further comprise an iterative graphic generation loop.

sources.title: System and Method for Real-Time, Local-First Artificial Intelligence Guidance During Live Conversations [US20260368216A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Disclosed are computer systems and methods for providing AI assistance based on audio input in real time. The assistance may comprise suggested responses to a guided participant during a conversation in response to other conversation participant(s). Generating the suggested response may include receiving audio input through a network connection, transcribing the audio input into a text transcript, identifying an intent within the text transcript, querying a vector database to retrieve relevant database content based on the intent, prompting a LLM to generate a response based on the intent and the relevant database content, and presenting the response in real time. Generating the response may also include querying a local semantic cache to search for semantically-similar text. When semantically-similar text is found, the cached response associated with the semantically-similar text may be presented. Otherwise, the LLM may be instructed to generate a new response.

sources.title: RETRIEVING DATA FROM RELATIONAL DATABASES USING LLM-BASED STRUCTURED QUERY GENERATION FROM NATURAL LANGUAGE QUERY [EP4841461A1]
sources.abstract: State of the art techniques have limitations is understanding intent of the natural language query in context of available database schema. This leads to generation of inappropriate structured query, effectively resulting in inappropriate data retrieval from database. A method for retrieving data from relational databases using LLM-based structured query generation from natural language query is provided. A first instance of LLM supports a schema mapping module while a second instance of LLM supports a query generation module. The SQL query generation utilizes ensemble of methods during query building for searching the database, wherein a full-text search, substring search, and semantic search is applied for searching short text fields of the relevant text-based columns, and wherein directly semantic search is applied to capture relevant content based on meaning, for searching long text fields of the relevant text-based columns if the approach used for short text field fails to retrieve intended data.

sources.title: PREVENTING DATA EXPOSURE DURING RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION [US20260359458A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Preventing data exposure during retrieval augmented generation, including: receiving, from a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model and based on a first input to the generative AI model comprising a request, an intermediate query for one or more tables, wherein the intermediate query is generated by the generative AI model as an intermediate step of a chain-of-thought for responding to the request; providing, to the generative AI model, a second input comprising a schema structure for an output of the intermediate query and an alias for the output of the intermediate query; receiving, from the generative AI model and based on the second input, a final query responsive to the request; and generating a response to the request by executing the final query.

sources.title: Targeted Behavioral Compliance Monitoring [US20260359766A1]
sources.abstract: A method for targeted behavioral compliance monitoring is described. Smart review entries corresponding to communications stored in an archive are clustered. Each smart review entry corresponds to a communication, by a monitored employee, that matched an infoTag. A query for the clustered smart review entries is received. The query is a natural language query. The query is performed on the clustered smart review entries using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Query results from the query are provided for display in a user interface (UI).

sources.title: UNIFIED GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) -BASED CHATBOT PLATFORM [US20260359472A1]
sources.abstract: Novel tools and techniques are provided for implementing a unified generative artificial intelligence ("AI") -based chatbot platform. The unified generative AI-based chatbot platform implements a single bot application that leverages context switching, role-based access control ("RBAC"), and an adaptive mechanism for dynamically choosing between cache augmented generation ("CAG") and retrieval augmented generation ("RAG") that can seamlessly connect to diverse backend data sources while ensuring stringent data separation and access control. In some examples, an application programming interface ("API") gateway is provided to manage and route requests to the appropriate data sources, which can simplify integration of new data sources and provide a centralized point for implementing security and monitoring features.

sources.title: MAINTAINING ACTIVE AND NON-ACTIVE VECTOR DATABASE SEARCH INDEXES [US20260359277A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method, according to one embodiment, comprises, in response to a determination that a first search index associated with a vector database exceeds a predetermined size threshold, performing a first process for rebuilding the first search index. The first process comprises monitoring performance and accuracy of the first search index while simultaneously modifying existing content in the vector database, and maintaining the first search index and a second search index. The maintaining comprises actively using the first search index for searching the vector database while building the second search index in a non-active state based on the modification of the existing content in the vector database. The first process further comprises, in response to a determination that the performance of the first search index falls below a threshold value, actively using the second search index for searching the vector database and rebuilding the first search index in the non-active state.

sources.title: EDGE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE EMULATOR ENGINE IN A CLOUD COMPUTING SYSTEM [US20260359087A1]
sources.abstract: Methods, systems, and computer storage media for providing edge artificial intelligence emulation using an edge artificial intelligence emulator engine in an artificial intelligence (AI) system are described. Edge artificial intelligence emulation refers to the set of processes, tools, and frameworks that oversee the configuration, execution, monitoring, and optimization of the edge AI emulation. The edge artificial intelligence emulator engine is designed to help users optimize language model deployments in hybrid edge-cloud environments. Edge artificial intelligence emulator engine via an edge artificial intelligence emulator supports evaluating different language model components, including frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) databases, retrievers, cloud backup strategies, and orchestration techniques, to determine the best configuration for a given hardware setup. Edge artificial intelligence emulator engine automates performance trade-off profiles evaluation of various component combinations to optimize edge AI systems. The edge artificial intelligence emulation engine generates an orchestrator and a performance trade-off profile to provide an AI system.

sources.title: DISTRIBUTED STORAGE ARCHITECTURE WITH AUTOMATED VIRTUALIZED ENVIRONMENT PROVISIONING AND CONTENT-INDEXED FILE MANAGEMENT [US20260359263A1]
sources.abstract: A file parsing and indexing system for training Large Language Models (LLMs) identifies a file type scope of a file deposited into a monitored location, comprising a specific file type, a general file type indicating multipart or single-part format, and file characteristics. The system parses the file into constituent components using a file parser tailored to the specific file type, extracts text or metadata from the components, and generates underlying contextual information comprising source site of collection, owner and author, collection details, and relationships to other files. The system creates structured index files containing the extracted text, metadata, and generated contextual information for LLM refinement training or retrieval augmented generation.

sources.title: AUTOMATED DESIGN VALIDATION FOR ELECTRIC POWER TRANSMISSION AND DISTRIBUTION INFRASTRUCTURE [US20260359515A1]
sources.abstract: A system performs an automated design validation process for electric power transmission and distribution infrastructure designs. A design validation bot applies a language model to generate validation schemas based on regulations for electric power transmission and distribution infrastructure (e.g., standards documents). In response to a request to validate a design package comprising a design for electric power transmission and distribution infrastructure and other data associated with the design, the design validation bot employs pre-processing tools to segment the design into semantically-coherent segments and extract text from the design package. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation process is performed in which the design validation bot identifies and retrieves relevant validation schema(s) and prompts the language model to validate the design package against the relevant validation schema(s) and generate a design validation report for the design package. The design validation bot incorporates user feedback at different stages to fine-tune the design validation process.

sources.title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR GENERATING COMPLETE AND CONTEXTUALLY ACCURATE RESPONSES USING HIERARCHICAL DOCUMENT CHUNKING AND RETRIEVAL [US20260359304A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    According to an aspect of the present disclosure, a computer-implemented method for generating complete and contextually accurate responses in a retrieval-augmented generation system using a pretrained generative artificial intelligence (AI) model is presented. A method may include modifying the query based on a determined relevance. A method may include parsing a plurality of electronic documents to identify hierarchical structures of each electronic document of the plurality of electronic documents. A method may include converting the hierarchical structures into one or more data chunks based on content within the hierarchical structures. A method may include retrieving one or more of the data chunks based on the modified query. A method may include receiving as output from the pretrained generative AI model a response based at least in part on the modified query and the retrieved one or more data chunks.

sources.title: System and Method for Litigation Intelligence Using Testimony, Court Filings, and Legal Authority [US20260359908A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A system and method are disclosed for integrated litigation intelligence, where testimonial evidence is analyzed alongside court filings, discovery materials, legal research databases, and real-time data streams to support dynamic case preparation and trial strategy. The system ingests deposition and trial transcripts, docket filings, legal authority (e.g., statutes, caselaw), and related materials to construct structured representations of the factual and procedural record. Using rule-based logic, retrieval-augmented generation, and generative AI, the system synthesizes narratives, drafts cross- and direct-examination outlines, identifies evidentiary gaps, and generates strategy documents aligned with legal standards. In some embodiments, the system monitors live testimony, updates outlines on the fly, and recommends follow-up questions or exhibits. It may also detect contradictions, align testimony to claims or defenses, and support expert consistency checks or appellate workflows. By linking testimony with filings and authority, the system enables more coherent, adaptive, and law-aware litigation strategy across the full case lifecycle.

sources.title: METHOD FOR ASSIGNING A SEMANTIC CONCEPT TO A PREVIOUSLY UNSEEN DATA ASSET [EP4838381A1]
sources.abstract: [0001]    A computer-implemented method assigns a semantic concept to a new data asset by: enriching (1) the data assets metadata I (tokenizing labels (A1), expanding acronyms (A2), leveraging (A3) a knowledge graph (11)/databases (14), generating descriptions (A4)); retrieving (2) candidate concepts and similarity scores via, e.g., vector database (13) searches comparing enriched metadata embeddings with concept descriptor embeddings; determining (3) a first ranking based on similarity scores; determining (4) at least a second ranking using a neural network (12b) processing the first ranking and enriched metadata; and storing a proposed mapping (O) based on at least the second ranking in a knowledge graph (11).

sources.title: Multimodal retrieval augmented generation [US12792647B1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A retrieval augmented generation (RAG) system determines, based on a query, an audio embedding type or a text embeddings type to use to filter an embeddings store, wherein the embedding store includes embeddings of the audio embedding type and the text embeddings type in a vector space. The RAG system obtains, from a filtered portion of the embeddings store, embeddings based on similarity scores between the plurality of embeddings and a representation of the query in the vector space. The RAG system obtains embedding source data from which a selected one of the plurality of embeddings of the embeddings store have been generated, wherein the embedding source data is source audio data or transcribed source audio data used to generate the embeddings in the embeddings store. The RAG system provides the query and the embedding source data for the selected embedding to the multimodal LLM.

sources.title: INDEX-BASED RETRIEVAL TECHNIQUES FOR RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION [EP4838375A1]
sources.abstract: A computer-implemented method includes receiving a natural language query that specifies a plurality of categories and data elements, and providing, to a Large Language Model (LLM), a first prompt comprising the natural language query and context metadata characterizing the categories and the data elements in a dataset. The context metadata comprises key-value pairs, where the keys include categories in the dataset, and the values include corresponding data elements in the dataset. The LLM outputs keywords identified in the natural language query based on the context metadata. One or more entries in the dataset are identified that contain data elements corresponding to the keywords. A second prompt comprising the received natural language query, the keywords, and one or more indexes to the one or more identified entries in the dataset is provided to the LLM, which outputs a generated output based on the identified entries in the dataset.

sources.title: Method of collecting contextual behavioral data within digital narrative intelligence environments [US12792581B1]
sources.abstract: A computer-implemented narrative intelligence system and method for managing digital artifacts and harvesting contextualized collaborator behaviors to support AI-assisted information management and model training. Content and collaborator interactions are organized into a narrative structure of sequenceable stories rendered on axis-based graphical timelines, where artifacts, events, and collaborator states are indexed, linked, and tokenized. Behavioral signals extracted from the narrative context are used to (i) enrich prompt construction and retrieval-augmented generation, (ii) curate and contextualize training datasets, and (iii) propose context-aware AI agents and interventions. The storytelling interface aligns visual, temporal, and relational cues with machine-learning workflows to produce narratively grounded behavioral data for fine-tuning models and enabling context-sensitive information navigation.

sources.title: Artificial intelligence-based networking using agents built on large language models (LLMs) [US12792640B1]
sources.abstract: Systems and methods for an AI-driven networking platform generate policy-controlled introductions via an LLM agent. User accounts store profile text, network strategy elements (goals, tasks, events, candidate introductions), and primary connections defining relationships and spheres of influence with connection types and strength rankings. For a target account, processors identify a first account having a primary relationship and determine candidate second accounts connected to the first but lacking a primary relationship with the target. The agent constructs an augmented model input comprising a system prompt specifying constraints and privacy rules, retrieved context, and a query derived from the target's strategy. The agent performs retrieval-augmented generation by embedding and semantically searching sources permitted by privacy rules, executes an LLM with low-rank adaptation modules, and outputs a recommendation. Using a tool-interface protocol, the agent automatically transmits notifications and orchestrates a double-opt-in introduction workflow. Outcomes and feedback update matching models, agent memory, and policies.

draft.summary: Research activity on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has grown very fast: 2,391 works in 2024, 8,632 in 2025 (+261%), and 15,610 by late October 2026 against 6,533 a year earlier, so momentum is still building [S1, S2]. Patent filings show a similar rise (2,212 in 2025; 2,738 by late October 2026 vs 1,663 a year earlier), covering context compression, vector indexing, security and multimodal use [P1, P2, P3, P4]. Market evidence is real but mostly small: a $21.4M acquisition (Nuclia) by Progress Software, plus several small companies describing RAG products, one with zero revenue [M1, M3, M5]. The main uncertainty is reliability: silent pipeline degradation, retrieval-quality dependence, security exposure and thin evidence for agentic RAG [R1, R2, R3, R4]. Research and patent volume is not commercial success, and several Science findings were weakened by the Risk challenges [C1, C2, C5]. Large-cap links are loose, as their excerpts do not discuss RAG specifically [M7].
draft.plain_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation lets an AI look up documents before answering, so it makes fewer things up. Research papers and patent filings on it are growing very fast and some small software companies are selling it. The main thing that could hold it back is reliability: these systems can quietly return wrong or insecure results, and that is hard to detect.

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Research and patent counts are still rising in 2026, and filings cover indexing, compression and vector databases. Small companies report RAG products and one acquisition occurred, but the evidence does not show paying-customer scale. Several of the products are early-stage or pre-revenue.

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Evaluation, silent degradation and retrieval quality are unresolved, and the evaluation metrics are fragmented. Whether tooling that addresses these becomes a durable product category is not shown by the findings. Patent and paper growth suggests continued competition, not a settled winner.

horizons.label: assumption
horizons.assessment: No finding addresses the 3-5 year commercial outcome. It is unclear whether RAG remains a distinct layer or is absorbed into larger AI platforms; the findings are silent on this.

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: RAG becomes a standard production component. Research and patent growth continue, and tooling for indexing, compression, governance and evaluation finds paying enterprise customers, as signalled by acquisitions and product launches by small software vendors.

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: RAG is widely used and keeps spreading into domains and multimodal inputs, but value goes mostly to vendors that fix reliability, security and evaluation. Many small vendors have limited revenue, and growth in papers and patents does not translate evenly into earnings.

bear.label: forecast
bear.narrative: Silent failures, retrieval-quality limits, security exposure and weak evidence for agentic designs hold back high-stakes deployment (healthcare, legal, industrial). Capabilities are absorbed into general platforms, and small vendors struggle to find revenue.
